theme: 3 terms for shared data in SwiftUI: the observable class, its announcing property and the view that owns it

terms.definition: A protocol for a class whose changes can update the views that watch it.
terms.example: Make the Cart an ObservableObject, so the screen can watch it.

terms.definition: A property wrapper that announces every change of a property to the views that watch it.
terms.example: Add Published to the total, or the view will never update.

terms.definition: A property wrapper that makes a view create and own an observable object for the whole life of the view.
terms.example: Use StateObject, so the view keeps the same Cart after a redraw.

video.title: ObservableObject, Published & StateObject | Day 151
video.description:
Learn to explain how SwiftUI views watch a class: ObservableObject, Published & StateObject, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
ObservableObject - A protocol for a class whose changes can update the views that watch it.
Published - A property wrapper that announces every change of a property to the views that watch it.
StateObject - A property wrapper that makes a view create and own an observable object for the whole life of the view.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain ObservableObject, Published and StateObject in English?

dialogue.title: The cart will not update

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my cart screen does not update when the total changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. It is a class, and the view watches it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then check the property. Without Published, the view never hears about the change.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I forgot it! Now I put Published before `total`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Every Published property tells the views when it changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It updates now. My teammate says I should use a plain `var` for `cart`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. A plain `var` creates a new `Cart` on every redraw. Use StateObject.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So StateObject keeps one object alive for the view?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The view owns it, and the same object stays for the whole life of the view.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That explains my reset bug. The total went back to zero.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. ObservableObject plus Published plus StateObject, and the screen is stable.
